subject: Television & Streaming
title: Saturday Night Live and Political Satire
description: Learn Saturday Night Live and Political Satire in one minute.

hook.text: Since 1975, Saturday Night Live has mocked every American president. Political satire became a television tradition.

buildup.text: Tina Fey's 2008 Sarah Palin impression was so effective that polls showed it shaped how voters saw the real candidate.

discovery.text: SNL proved that comedy can shape political narratives.

twist.text: Politicians began appearing on the show themselves, trying to control the joke.

climax.text: Political satire on television occupies a unique space: it's dismissed as comedy but functions as the most widely.

punchline.text: The joke is always on the politician. Unless they're in on it.

quiz.question: How did Tina Fey's Sarah Palin impression demonstrate television satire's power?
options: Polls showed it influenced voters' actual perceptions of Palin
